title: Direct Bandgap Light Emission from Strained Germanium Nanowires Coupled with High-Q Nanophotonic Cavities

nodes.label: Silicon photonics needs a CMOS-compatible on-chip light source, and germanium is indirect-gap
Whether high tensile strain plus a high-Q cavity can bring Ge to net optical gain is unsettled, with conflicting lasing reports
Above 2% uniaxial tensile strain should make Ge effectively direct-gap and, in a matched DBR cavity, give strong tunable direct-gap emission
n-type Ge-on-insulator, 1e19 cm-3 phosphorus, in a 200 nm Ge / 25 nm Al2O3 / 850 nm SiO2 / Si stack

attrs.reason: in-situ doped Ge with a sacrificial oxide that can be undercut

nodes.label: An 8 um x 700 nm nanowire widening to 13.7 um tapers and 20 um pads, with 10-period curved DBR mirrors of 380 nm period and 21% duty cycle about 30 um apart
Strain levels 0, 1.95 and 2.37% in otherwise identical cavities, and pump power from 1 to about 48 mW
Let capillary drying pull the released wire back onto the SiO2 and then passivate with ALD, so heat can leave the wire

attrs.note: solves the thermal failure of the free-standing device

nodes.label: One electron-beam lithography step and an HBr/Cl2 dry etch define wire, tapers and mirrors in the Ge layer
KOH undercut removes the sacrificial Al2O3 so the pads contract and amplify the 0.2% as-grown strain into the wire
About 10 nm of conformal Al2O3 by atomic layer deposition over the reattached wire
The fabricated device reproduces the design: an 8 um wire between tapered pads with curved DBR stacks in a 200 nm Ge layer
The wire carries about 2.4% uniform uniaxial tensile strain along its length, from 0.2% in the as-grown layer
Capillary drying reattaches the wire to the SiO2 by van der Waals contact, restoring a heat path and optical confinement
Tensile strain narrows the gap and pulls the direct valley down, while the wire-to-pad strain gradient builds a pseudo-heterostructure that confines carriers in the wire
Direct-gap photoluminescence redshifts from ~1560 nm unstrained to ~1960-1990 nm at 1.95-2.37% strain, more than 400 nm of tuning
The cavity delivers resonances with a 24.6 nm free spectral range and a fitted Q of 2020, and the reattached device survives more than ten times the pump power of the free-standing one

attrs.condition: 980 nm CW and 1550 nm pulsed pumping

nodes.label: Net optical gain stays negative and falls with pump power, though the 2.37% device beats the 1.95% one at every power
The dominant loss is inter-valence-band absorption, which overtakes conduction-band free-carrier loss above ~6e18 cm-3
Strain plus a high-Q cavity gives strong, widely tunable direct-gap Ge emission, but free-carrier and inter-valence-band absorption hold net gain negative, so no lasing is seen

nodes.label: Tensile strain narrows the Ge bandgap and lowers the direct valley relative to the indirect one
Earlier reports claim lasing in Ge at comparable strain and doping levels
Empirical pseudopotential method used to compute the gain and the individual loss terms
Carroll et al. report pump-induced absorption in strained Ge
No sign of lasing is seen despite strain and doping comparable to the earlier lasing reports, in line with the pump-induced absorption reported elsewhere
The 2.37% emission peak falls beyond the extended-InGaAs detection limit above 2000 nm, so its true position and intensity are not measured

notes: A device paper whose spine forks after the strained structure (g12) into an emission branch (g14 -> g15 -> g16) and a gain branch (g17 -> g18), with the negative-result conclusion g19 joining them. g7 is DES/route with purpose=decouple because the capillary reattachment exists only to give the wire a heat path, which is what makes the 10x pump-power range possible at all. Audits: a1 (the Raman map shows 0.5-0.8% residual strain in the pads where the FEM map reads zero, and the pseudo-heterostructure argument rests on that contrast), a2 (the 2.37% spectrum carries no resonance comb, so the Q and free-spectral-range claims come from the 1.95% device only), a3 (the carrier density in the gain-model comparison is itself fitted to the same theory, making the F5b agreement partly circular). h6 records that PL intensity does not keep rising with strain and that the 2.37% peak is clipped by the detector limit (limg1). h10 notes the caption/text conflict over the 1.95% probe wavelength (1961 vs 1923 nm). F5c is model output alone, flagged in h12. Lost: the SI thermal simulations, the mirror design, the confinement factor of 0.37 and the carrier-density calculation.

changes: Spine cycle removed. g17 -> g18 supports and g18 -> g17 explains formed a two-node loop, so the spine was not a stage-ordered path. Kept g17 -> g18 (the negative measured gain is what licenses the loss identification) and moved the explains edge to g18 -> g19, which is what the paper's conclusion actually says: inter-valence-band and free-carrier absorption hold the gain negative, so no lasing is seen. g18 now reaches the conclusion under its own rel.

h7 and h10: provenance derived -> measured. Both read the paper's own reduction of data in the same panel (a Lorentzian fit; net gain against pump power) with no OBS parent in this graph, and v04 requires an incoming derives edge for derived.

a3: provenance derived -> computed. The carrier-density abscissa this node reads IS model output - a calculation of absorbed power plus a fit to theory - which is exactly what provenance=computed records, and it needs no derives edge.

h2: image_note sharpened. The undercut region sits at ~0 nm while the wafer outside runs +20 nm on the right and +30 to +38 nm on the left, so '20-25 nm below' is the right-hand reference; the trench-edge notches fall below -50 nm.

panel_checks.note: Exactly right and the most consequential audit here. In F4a the 1.95% trace (red) is a dense comb of sharp resonances peaking at ~2700, while the 2.37% trace (blue) is a smooth envelope peaking at ~1100 with no comb anywhere. The caption credits both strained wires with high-Q resonances, so image_support=contradicts is the correct grade, and the Q and free-spectral-range claims do rest on the 1.95% device alone. h6's numbers (0% ~280 near 1560 nm, 1.95% comb maxima ~2700, 2.37% ~1100) and limg1's detector-limit band above 2000 nm also check out on this panel.

Confirmed on both panels. F3b (FEM) shows the pads black at essentially zero with faint red only at the taper fillets; F3c (Raman) shows the pads at a clear dark red, about 0.5-0.8% on the same 0-2.4% scale. The paper's 'the Raman result matches the FEM simulation' holds for the wire and not for the pads, and it is the wire-to-pad contrast that the pseudo-heterostructure argument in g14 rests on. h3's note that the wire is clipped pure white at the top of the scale is also right.

F5a reads -350 (2.37%) and -520 (1.95%) at 5 mW and -1250 and -1970 at 22 mW, negative throughout - the node's numbers exactly. The 1.95% error bars at 22 mW span about -1600 to -2380, and the two series do nearly touch at 5 mW, as the image_note says.

review.audit_summary: 3 audits plus a DSC/limitation and a DSC/comparison - inside budget, and unusually well placed for a negative-result paper. Each hits a different link: a1 the strain-contrast premise of the pseudo-heterostructure (g14), a2 the cavity claim (g16), a3 the circularity of the gain-model comparison (g18). a2 is the only one graded contradicts and deserves it - the caption claims resonances for a trace that has none. a1 and a3 are correctly graded shown, because what they report is what the panels plainly display; the fault is in the text's gloss, not in the figures. limg1 is a genuine method limit (the 2.37% peak is clipped by the extended-InGaAs cutoff) and bounds g15 rather than contradicting it. dcg1 is typed as DSC/comparison with verdict=conflict, correctly: the disagreement is with prior lasing reports, not with this paper's own data. Three further soft spots are kept on image_support rather than promoted: h6 partial (emission does not keep rising with strain), h7 partial (the fitted Q depends on the window), h11 partial (the EPM curve runs above the points near 2e19 cm-3), and h12's image_note records that F5c is model output alone with no measurement separating the two loss terms.
